instruction.text: Sort the numbers from the smallest at the top to the largest at the bottom.
Sort the decimals with one decimal place from the smallest at the top to the largest at the bottom.

hint.text:
All the decimals have the same digit in the ones place, so the digits in the first decimal place have to be compared.

For example, here, both decimals have a 4 in the ones place, but the decimal above has a larger digit in the first decimal place than the decimal below:

4.2
4.1

Thus 4.2 is larger than 4.1.

instruction.text: Sort the decimals with two decimal places from the smallest at the top to the largest at the bottom.

hint.text:
All the decimals have the same digit in the ones place and in the first decimal place, so the digits in the second decimal place have to be compared to work out the value of the numbers.

For example, here, both decimals have a 4 in the ones place and a 1 in the first decimal place, but the decimal above has a larger digit in the second decimal place than the decimal below:

4.13
4.12

Thus 4.13 is larger than 4.12.
hint.sound:
All the decimals have the same digit in the ones place and in the first decimal place, so the digits in the second decimal place have to be compared to work out the value of the numbers.

For example, here, both decimals have a 4 in the ones place and a 1 in the first decimal place, but the decimal above has a larger digit in the second decimal place than the decimal below. Thus 4.13 is larger than 4.12.

instruction.text: Sort the decimals with three decimal places from the smallest at the top to the largest at the bottom.

hint.text:
All the decimals have the same digit in the ones place and in the first and second decimal place, so the digits in the third decimal place have to be compared to work out the value of the numbers.

For example, here, both decimals have a 4 in the ones place, a 1 in the first decimal place and a 2 in the second decimal place, but the decimal above has a larger digit in the third decimal place than the decimal below:

4.125
4.124

Thus 4.125 is larger than 4.124.
hint.sound:

For example, here, both decimals have a 4 in the ones place, a 1 in the first decimal place and a 2 in the second decimal place, but the decimal above has a larger digit in the third decimal place than the decimal below. Thus 4.125 is larger than 4.124.

instruction.text: To be able to order decimal numbers more easily, it is helpful if they all have the same number of decimal places. Fill in missing decimal places with zeros.

trainers.hint: You can add as many 0s to the end of a decimal number as you need to make it have the same number of decimal places as other ones.

instruction.text: Now sort the decimals from the smallest at the top to the largest at the bottom.

trainers.hint: Compare the decimal numbers place by place. If the digit in the ones place is the same for two numbers, compare the digits in the tenths place and so on until the digits are different.
